name: The Spinanes
label: Merge
lede: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf made a Portland duo out of one guitar and one drum kit, and it handed Sub Pop its first No. 1 on college radio. Then Plouf took a second job drumming for Built to Spill, and Gates moved to Chicago.

eras.title: Two people, no bass player
eras.text: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf made a full band's worth of noise with a guitar and a drum kit. By their own account their first big stage was the International Pop Underground Convention, K Records' gathering in Olympia.

years.h: Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf start a band with no bass player
years.p: Gates sings and plays guitar, Plouf drums, and the Portland, Oregon duo never adds a bassist in its original run.

years.h: The Spinanes play one of their first shows at the IPU convention
years.p: At K Records' International Pop Underground Convention in Olympia, Washington, in August 1991, Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf play one of their first shows. Their song Jad Fair Drives Women Wild lands on the convention compilation.
years.xp: The song is named for [[Jad Fair|be4a8e65-a7ba-474c-989b-ed16e51c1a39]] of [[Half Japanese|18dc6bd7-9caa-4c2d-a2fc-e9546ebda6a4]]. K Records put the IPU compilation out in 1991.

years.h: IMP Records puts out two Spinanes singles
years.p: The small Portland label IMP issues both, and Merge gathers them years later as Imp Years.

eras.title: Sub Pop gets its college-radio No. 1
eras.text: Sub Pop was still selling grunge when it signed a Portland duo with no bass player. The Spinanes' first album went to the top of the college charts and put Noel, Jonah and Me on MTV's 120 Minutes.

years.cap: Scott Plouf and Rebecca Gates, c. 1993
years.h: Sub Pop signs the duo and releases Spitfire
years.p: The Seattle label that built its name on grunge signs Rebecca Gates and Scott Plouf and puts out the single Spitfire.

years.cap: Scott Plouf and Rebecca Gates, c. 1993
years.src: Wikipedia: Manos (album) · Wikipedia: The Spinanes · NPR
yt: Live at the Middle East, Cambridge MA, Nov 3, 1993
years.h: Manos becomes Sub Pop's first No. 1 on college radio
years.p: Newsday's Ira Robbins ranks the Spinanes' debut ninth among the best albums of 1993. Not everyone agrees on what it is.
years.xp:
Robert Christgau called Manos a dud. Pitchfork later gave it an 8.5 and the Chicago Tribune gave it three stars.

NPR's 2012 profile of Gates describes it as the first Sub Pop record to hit No. 1 on CMJ's college chart. The album's Wikipedia page words the claim more broadly, as the first album on an independent label to top the US college charts.

yt: Noel, Jonah and Me, TV performance and interview, May 1994
years.h: Noel, Jonah and Me lands on MTV's 120 Minutes
years.p: The second single from Manos gets heavy college and alternative airplay. A video for the third, Sunday, follows in 1994.
The Spinanes contribute the song to the Kill Rock Stars compilation.

eras.title: Plouf takes a second drum seat
eras.text: Strand was the last Spinanes record as a duo. Scott Plouf had started drumming for Boise's Built to Spill, who were signed to Warner Bros.

yt: Lines and Lines, live at Bottom of the Hill, 1998
years.p: The second Spinanes album for Sub Pop is bookended by the singles Madding and Lines and Lines, with John Moen also on backing vocals.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Smith and Moen for backup vocals. Gates played Lines and Lines live at Bottom of the Hill in San Francisco on September 26, 1998.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Spinanes · Wikipedia: Built to Spill
years.h: Plouf starts drumming for Built to Spill with the Spinanes still going
years.p: Around 1996 he joins [[Doug Martsch|42c520b5-4992-4aab-9f3f-542addcde686]]'s [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]], by then on Warner Bros.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Spinanes · Wikipedia: Built to Spill · AllMusic
years.h: Plouf quits the Spinanes and stays with Built to Spill until 2012
years.p: Per Wikipedia he leaves in 1997 to become Built to Spill's permanent drummer, which leaves Rebecca Gates without one.
years.xp: Plouf drummed on Built to Spill's Keep It Like a Secret, Ancient Melodies of the Future, You in Reverse and There Is No Enemy.

eras.title: Chicago, with Tortoise's John McEntire
eras.text: Rebecca Gates moved to Chicago and rebuilt the Spinanes as a trio. John McEntire of Tortoise co-produced the third album, and the name did not last much longer.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Spinanes · Wikipedia: Arches and Aisles
yt: Eleganza, live at Bottom of the Hill, 1998
years.h: Gates moves to Chicago and builds a trio around Bolme and Busher
years.p: Rebecca Gates makes the Spinanes a three-piece with bassist [[Joanna Bolme|21f4bc79-8b24-4aee-85b3-22f46cf2e5d2]] and drummer [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]], the first bassist in the band's history.
years.xp: Bolme went on to play bass in [[Stephen Malkmus|eaefd603-84c1-4db4-a72b-0cb718a0cc07]]'s Jicks and in [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]]. Busher spent years filling out [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]]'s live sound on drums, percussion and trumpet, and later formed [[French Toast|f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480]] with James Canty.

years.h: Arches and Aisles brings in McEntire and Sam Prekop
years.p: Recorded at Easley McCain in Memphis and at McEntire's Soma studio in Chicago, with [[Sam Prekop|33175dbe-db6c-4f0b-a4c6-9addcd403186]] of [[The Sea and Cake|74171cb6-1ff8-42bd-be8a-96660c22e3e0]] singing on it.
years.xp: AllMusic called it the group's least confining, most listenable record. Trouser Press called it a superlative album of quietly remarkable songs. In 2016 Pitchfork placed it at No. 46 on its list of the best Pacific Northwest indie rock albums.

years.h: Merge collects the early singles on Imp Years
years.p: The 2000 compilation is the Spinanes' first release on Merge Records.

years.h: Gates retires the Spinanes name and goes solo with Ruby Series
years.p: Her 2001 solo debut ends the band. NPR notes John McEntire of Tortoise worked on it with her.

eras.title: The long way back to Manos
eras.text: After 2001 Rebecca Gates shifted toward visual art and design, curating exhibitions and giving lectures, and worked with the Future of Music Coalition. In 2018 Merge reissued Manos.

years.cap: Rebecca Gates singing in an OPB Music session, Portland, 2012
years.h: Gates returns after 11 years with 17 players on The Float
years.p: Rebecca Gates & the Consortium is her second solo album, with players from [[Quasi|3df29542-402a-49a5-ae1f-82f936184b3b]], [[Wild Flag|4473e47b-81bb-47af-8cb0-1cad6f68d8bc]] and [[The Decemberists|97b1142f-c71e-4971-8736-4a8ceaf6b4c3]].
years.xp: NPR says the Consortium is 17 musicians. For touring she works with Joanna Bolme on bass, Rebecca Cole on keys and Ji Tanzer on drums.

years.h: Merge reissues Manos in a deluxe edition
years.p: Merge Records puts the Spinanes' 1993 debut back out, and Vogue runs an interview with Rebecca Gates on December 5, 2018.

sources.title: NPR: Rebecca Gates, The Spinanes Star, Floats On
